question:
[6 pts] Given two documents:
• D1: "the cat sat on the mat"
• D2: "the dog sat on the log"

(a) Calculate the TF-IDF weight of the word "cat" in D1. (2 pts)
(b) Build the TF-IDF vectors for D1 and D2. (2 pts)
(c) Calculate the Cosine Similarity between D1 and D2. (2 pts)
(Use log base 2, N = 2 documents. Show all steps.)
answer:
(a) TF-IDF of "cat" in D1:
• TF(cat, D1) = count / total = 1/6 ≈ 0.167
• IDF(cat) = log₂(N / df) = log₂(2/1) = 1.0
• TF-IDF(cat, D1) = 0.167 × 1.0 = 0.167

(b) TF-IDF Vectors:
• Shared words (the, sat, on): df = 2 → IDF = log₂(2/2) = 0 → eliminated!
• Unique to D1 (cat, mat): df = 1 → IDF = 1.0
• Unique to D2 (dog, log): df = 1 → IDF = 1.0

Vocabulary order: [the, cat, sat, on, mat, dog, log]
• D1 = [0, 1/6, 0, 0, 1/6, 0, 0]
• D2 = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1/6, 1/6]

(c) Cosine Similarity:
• cos(D1, D2) = (D1 · D2) / (‖D1‖ × ‖D2‖)
• D1 · D2 = 0 (no overlapping non-zero dimensions)
• cos(D1, D2) = 0

💡 Key insight: TF-IDF eliminates common words via IDF=0, so the only surviving dimensions are unique words — which don't overlap between D1 and D2.
explanation:
评分标准 / Marking Rubric:
• (a) 正确计算 TF 和 IDF 各 1 分 (2 pts)
• (b) 正确识别共同词 IDF=0 并构建向量 (2 pts)
• (c) 正确使用余弦公式并得出结论 (2 pts)

公式速记: TF = count/total; IDF = log(N/df); TF-IDF = TF × IDF; Cosine = dot(A,B)/(|A|×|B|)

question:
[6 pts] Explain the Scaled Dot-Product Attention mechanism in Transformer.

(a) Write the complete attention formula. (2 pts)
(b) Define Q, K, V — what does each represent and how is it obtained? (2 pts)
(c) Explain why we divide by √d_k. What goes wrong if we skip this step? (2 pts)
answer:
(a) Formula:
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QKT / √d_k) × V

(b) Q, K, V Definitions:
• Q (Query): "What am I looking for?" — obtained via linear transform WQ
• K (Key): "What information do I offer?" — obtained via linear transform WK
• V (Value): "What is my actual content?" — obtained via linear transform WV
Each input token is projected into three different vectors through learned weight matrices.

(c) Why divide by √d_k:
When d_k is large (e.g., 64), Q·KT produces values with large variance (~d_k).
• Without scaling: softmax → [0.99, 0.005, 0.005] (near one-hot) → gradients ≈ 0 → training fails
• With scaling: softmax → [0.4, 0.3, 0.3] (smooth distribution) → healthy gradients → stable training

Dividing by √d_k normalizes the variance back to ~1, keeping softmax in a useful gradient range.
explanation:
评分标准 / Marking Rubric:
• (a) 完整公式含 softmax, QKT, √d_k, V (2 pts)
• (b) Q/K/V 含义 + 来源 W_Q, W_K, W_V (2 pts)
• (c) 解释大维度→大方差→softmax过尖→梯度消失 (2 pts)

拓展: Multi-Head = h个独立头并行; 交叉注意力中 Q来自解码器, K/V来自编码器

question:
[6 pts] Explain BERT's two pre-training tasks.

(a) Describe MLM (Masked Language Modelling) and the 80/10/10 masking strategy. (3 pts)
(b) Describe NSP (Next Sentence Prediction). (1 pt)
(c) Explain why the 80/10/10 split is necessary — what goes wrong if all 15% are replaced with [MASK]? (2 pts)
answer:
(a) MLM — Masked Language Modelling:
• Randomly select 15% of input tokens, then:
→ 80% replaced with [MASK] — model learns to predict from context
→ 10% replaced with a random word — prevents model from only reacting to [MASK]
→ 10% kept unchanged — forces model to maintain representations for all tokens

(b) NSP — Next Sentence Prediction:
• Input: Sentence A + Sentence B
• Binary classification: IsNext (50%) vs NotNext (50%)
• Purpose: learn sentence-level relationships (needed for QA, NLI, etc.)
• Total Loss = LMLM + LNSP

(c) Why 80/10/10 (not 100% [MASK]):
If all selected tokens → [MASK]:
• During fine-tuning/inference, [MASK] token never appears in input
• Model would only learn to predict when it sees [MASK] → train-test mismatch
• 10% random word: forces model to consider ALL tokens, not just [MASK] positions
• 10% unchanged: model must produce good representations even for "normal" tokens
explanation:
评分标准 / Marking Rubric:
• (a) 正确描述 15% 选择 + 80/10/10 三种处理 (3 pts)
• (b) 正确描述 NSP 的输入和目标 (1 pt)
• (c) 解释训练-推理不匹配问题 (2 pts)

补充: BERT-base: 12层/768维/12头/110M; Encoder-only; [CLS]用于分类; [SEP]分隔句子

question:
[6 pts] Describe the RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline.

(a) List all 6 steps of the RAG pipeline in correct order and briefly explain each. (3 pts)
(b) Explain TWO key advantages of RAG over using a pure LLM. (2 pts)
(c) Does RAG completely eliminate hallucinations? Why or why not? (1 pt)
answer:
(a) RAG Pipeline — 6 Steps:
① Parse — Convert documents (PDF/HTML/DOCX) into plain text
② Chunk — Split text into blocks (256–512 tokens, 50-token overlap)
③ Embed — Convert chunks into dense vectors using an embedding model
④ Retrieve — Query → embedding → cosine similarity → find top-k relevant chunks
⑤ Augment — Insert retrieved chunks into the LLM prompt template
⑥ Generate — LLM produces an answer grounded in the retrieved documents

(b) Two Advantages over Pure LLM:
• Solves Knowledge Cutoff: LLMs only know training data up to a cutoff date. RAG retrieves current documents at runtime → up-to-date answers.
• Reduces Hallucination + Provides Source Attribution: Answers grounded in real documents; can cite sources ("According to Ch.3, p.45...") → verifiable and trustworthy.

(c) Does RAG eliminate hallucinations?
No. RAG reduces but does not eliminate hallucinations. If the retriever fetches wrong or irrelevant chunks, the LLM may still generate incorrect answers based on poor context.
explanation:
评分标准 / Marking Rubric:
• (a) 6步顺序正确 + 每步1句解释 (3 pts, 0.5 per step)
• (b) 两个优点解释清楚 (2 pts, 1 each)
• (c) 明确回答"不能完全消除" + 原因 (1 pt)

区分: RAG ≠ Fine-tuning! RAG=运行时检索(不改模型权重); Fine-tuning=修改模型权重

question:
[6 pts] Model Compression and Memory Calculation.

(a) Compare Quantization, Pruning, and Knowledge Distillation: what each does and whether re-training is needed. (3 pts)
(b) Calculate the memory required for a 7B-parameter model in FP32, FP16, INT8, and INT4 formats. (2 pts)
(c) What is LoRA? How does it reduce the number of trainable parameters? (1 pt)
answer:
(a) Three Compression Techniques:
• Quantization: Reduces numerical precision (FP32 → INT8). ❌ No re-training needed. Example: BERT 1.36 GB → 340 MB (4× smaller)
• Pruning: Removes unimportant weights/neurons (sets to zero). ⚠️ Often needs re-training to recover accuracy. Example: Remove 90% weights → fine-tune
• Knowledge Distillation: Trains a small "student" model to mimic a large "teacher" model's soft probability outputs. ✅ Requires full training cycle. Example: BERT → DistilBERT (97% quality, 60% smaller)

Key: Quantization changes precision (not values); Pruning removes connections; Distillation creates a new model. All three can be combined.

(b) 7B Model Memory (Rule: N × bytes_per_param):
• FP32: 7B × 4 bytes = 28 GB
• FP16: 7B × 2 bytes = 14 GB
• INT8: 7B × 1 byte = 7 GB
• INT4: 7B × 0.5 bytes = 3.5 GB
📐 Formula: FP32=×4, FP16=×2, INT8=×1, INT4=×0.5

(c) LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation):
• Freezes the entire base model, only trains two small matrices: A (d×r) and B (r×d), where r ≪ d (typically r = 4–16)
• Parameter reduction: d² → 2dr (e.g., d=768, r=4: 590K → 6K per layer = 98% reduction)
• QLoRA = LoRA + 4-bit quantized base → enables fine-tuning 65B models on 48GB GPU
explanation:
评分标准 / Marking Rubric:
• (a) 三种方法各1分: 描述+是否重训 (3 pts)
• (b) 正确应用公式算出4种大小 (2 pts)
• (c) LoRA核心概念: 冻结基座 + 低秩分解 (1 pt)

必记公式: FP32=×4, FP16=×2, INT8=×1, INT4=×0.5 | LoRA: d²→2dr
